name: nc-permitted-subtrees-explicit-tag-invalid
description: The PKIX ASN.1 module declares its tagging as IMPLICIT (RFC 5280 Appendix A.1 'DEFINITIONS IMPLICIT TAGS'), so 'permittedSubtrees [0] GeneralSubtrees' is implicit-tagged: on the wire the GeneralSubtrees SEQUENCE's outer tag (0x30) is replaced by 0xA0. This certificate instead emits the field with EXPLICIT tagging — i.e. a context-specific [0] CONSTRUCTED wrapper *around* the GeneralSubtrees SEQUENCE — producing one extra SEQUENCE layer on the wire (A0 LL 30 LL ... instead of A0 LL ...). The extension is critical, so per RFC 5280 §4.2 a decoder that cannot parse it MUST reject the certificate; a strict DER decoder must also reject the explicit form as not matching the schema. A lenient decoder that accepts either tagging form will descend through the spurious wrapper and treat the constraint as permitting 'example.com', accepting the leaf in violation of the schema.
notes: Wire layout difference: implicit tagging emits 'A0 LL { 30 LL { 82 LL "example.com" } }'; explicit tagging here emits 'A0 LL { 30 LL { 30 LL { 82 LL "example.com" } } }' — one extra SEQUENCE before the first GeneralSubtree.

Symmetric to `general-name-context-class-mismatch-invalid` (wrong tag *class* on the inner GeneralName); this one keeps the class correct but breaks the implicit-vs-explicit contract at the outer subtree-list field.
